thread:
anya: Quick sync — proposal to merge the batching, caching, and quantization RFCs into one Optimize Toolkit PRD so we can ship a cohesive developer surface and rollout plan. Thoughts?

jordan: I like consolidation. Customers ask for a single set of recommendations, not 3 competing docs.

lee: +1. We should define clear guardrails so runtime doesn't choose risky quantization profiles by default.

nina: We need acceptance criteria that capture quality regressions. Suggest: automatic evals on canonical prompt set + human spot checks for top-5 customers.

sam: Also need SLOs: latency regression <= 5% p50, tail (p99) impact needs a hard limit, and a fall-back path if model quality drops > 1.5% on BLEU/ROUGE or customer-defined metric.

anya: Proposed launch criteria (first pass):
- Min: packaging of recommendations for small, medium, large workloads + reference configs
- Measurables: cost/unit reduction target of 18% for text-gen 2k seq; latency change <= +5% p50 vs baseline
- Safety: automated quality checks and canary rollout across 10% traffic, with automated rollback on regressions
- Docs & SDK: example config snippets for Hosted / Dedicated / Private

jordan: For the canary policy: prefer region-aware canaries and per-customer opt-in flag for Private installs. We should also expose a "quality threshold" field in the API for auto-fallback.

lee: Implementation note: caching changes will interact with batching. We need an integration test that simulates prefix reuse and KV cache hits to measure end-to-end latency & cost. Put that in acceptance tests.

nina: Edge cases to call out in PRD:
- very short prompts (<= 16 tokens) where batching adds overhead
- streaming responses + quantized paths mixing float and int kernels
- models loaded in low-memory mode hitting OOM under aggressive batching

sam: Ops requirements:
- monitoring: per-route token cost, p50/p95/p99 latency, quantized kernel error rate (inferred mismatches)
- alerting: quality regression, OOM spikes, sudden cost delta > 30%

anya: Scope negotiation: I propose Phase 1 (MVP) = recommendations + runtime flags + canary framework + core acceptance tests. Phase 2 = per-customer calibration tool, UI in Console, automated tuning by workload. Phase 1 must fit 6-week sprint.

jordan: Can we trim MVP to 4 weeks by focusing on Medium workloads and Hosted only, and postpone Dedicated/Private SDKs to Phase 2? That buys time.

lee: That's reasonable but Dedicated customers will push back. Suggest we prioritize Dedicated-compatible APIs but implement Dedicated adapters in Phase 2. Means API/schema stable, runtime hooks queued.

nina: For evaluations, I'll own the canonical prompt sets and build the auto-eval harness. Need sample customers (3) for manual checks.

sam: I'll draft the SRE runbook for rollback criteria and monitoring dashboards.

ops-bot: doc uploaded: https://redwood.docs/optimize-toolkit/draft-1759991111 (permissions: eng-platform, eng-ml, product)

anya: Next steps:
- jordan: write condensed PRD skeleton (acceptance criteria + rollout plan) by Tue
- nina: canonical prompts + eval harness draft by Wed
- lee: list runtime changes & test plan by Wed
- sam: initial runbook + alerts by Thu
- I'll consolidate into a single RFC for review next Fri

jordan: tagging customers for feedback: @acme-ai, @fintech-partner — can product reach out and gather 2 high-priority asks?

anya: yes, will ping them after PRD skeleton.

lee: tiny nit: include a short section on quantization governance (who signs off per-model). Important for Private installs.

nina: noted.

anya: Thanks all — will follow up with a calendar invite for RFC readout. :thumbsup:

lee: +1

sam: :rocket:
